snippet.description:
Is wanting to be rich selfish? Does making money require exploiting other people? Or can the pursuit of wealth actually benefit society?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In this episode, guest host Sally Herships speaks with philosopher Jason Brennan about his book, "Why It's OK to Want to Be Rich." Jason makes the case that both wanting money and earning money are signs that we’re creating value for society. In this conversation, they explore why society believes money corrupts relationships, what wealthy individuals owe to society, and the cultural differences around money and wealth.

This episode was produced in partnership with Vox's Future Perfect.

00:00 Intro
03:19 Wanting to be rich is good for society
14:27 Capitalism, winners, and losers
24:43 Wealth, taxes, and banking
34:25 Does capitalism require exploitation?
39:57 What do the rich owe society?

Host: Sally Herships, journalist and director of the audio program at Columbia University's Graduate School of Journalism. (Find Sally’s work here).

Guest: Jason Brennan, professor of philosophy and public affairs at Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business.

We would love to hear from you. To tell us what you thought of this episode, email us at thegrayarea@vox.com or leave us a voicemail at 1-800-214-5749. Your comments and questions help us make a better show.

Explore the story, power, and deeper meaning of Mahakali through a spiritual journey across Kalighat Temple, Dakshineswar Kali Temple, and Belur Math in Kolkata.

From the story of Raktabija and Maa Kali standing on Lord Shiva, to the devotion of Ramakrishna Paramhansa, this documentary explores Shakti Upasana, Shakta tradition, Kali Puja, Durga Puja, Tantra, bhakti, meditation, and Sanatan Dharma.

It also touches on themes connected to Raktabija & Shukracharya, Shakti Peethas, spiritual awakening, Maa Durga, Swami Vivekananda, and Indian spirituality.

A journey to understand why Mahakali is not just fierce, but also a powerful symbol of love, protection, and transformation.

Jai Maa Kali. 🙏

#mahakali #kolkata

Introduction to Organic Chemistry for Class 9 Chemistry Chapter 11 explains the fundamental concepts of organic chemistry, the chemistry of carbon-containing compounds. This video is designed for students following the Pakistani Matric curriculum, including FBISE, Punjab Board (PCTB), Sindh, and other provincial textbooks.

In this lesson, you will learn:

What organic chemistry is and why carbon is the foundation of organic compounds
The unique properties of carbon that make it ideal for forming diverse molecules
The difference between organic and inorganic compounds
Basic classification of organic compounds and functional groups
Simple examples of common organic compounds in daily life
How organic chemistry connects to real-world applications in medicine, plastics, and fuel

Organic chemistry is a crucial topic in Class 9 Chemistry, and mastering the basics will prepare you for more advanced topics in Class 10 and beyond. Whether you're studying for your school exams, preparing for FBISE board tests, or aiming to strengthen your chemistry fundamentals, this chapter provides essential knowledge.

This video follows the National Curriculum of Pakistan and aligns with textbooks used across all major education boards. The content is presented in clear, step-by-step explanations with examples relevant to Pakistani students.

If this video helped you understand organic chemistry better, please like, subscribe, and comment your questions below. Don't forget to turn on notifications so you don't miss our upcoming videos on more chemistry chapters!

Translation elongation and termination are critical steps in protein synthesis during which the ribosome adds amino acids to the growing polypeptide chain and finally releases the complete protein. This Class 12 Biology Chapter 19 video explains these fundamental processes that follow translation initiation.

In this comprehensive lesson, you will learn:

• How elongation factors facilitate the addition of amino acids to the ribosome
• The role of tRNA in delivering amino acids during protein synthesis
• How peptide bonds form between successive amino acids
• The significance of stop codons in translation termination
• How release factors recognize stop codons and release the finished protein
• Why these processes are essential for accurate protein production

Translation elongation and termination are essential concepts for FSc Part 2 students preparing for FBISE, Punjab Board, Sindh Board, KPK Board, and other Pakistani examination boards. Understanding these mechanisms is crucial for scoring well in your Intermediate Biology exams and mastering molecular biology.

This video follows the National Curriculum of Pakistan and PCTB textbook standards, making it perfect for students across all provinces. Whether you are studying from Punjab Curriculum and Textbook Board materials or preparing for competitive tests, this detailed explanation will strengthen your conceptual understanding.

Watch this video to build confidence in protein synthesis topics and improve your grades. Subscribe to our channel for more Class 12 Biology lessons covering all chapters. Like this video, leave your questions in the comments, and share with fellow students preparing for their exams.
